title: British Columbia Gazette, 5 July 1973: Sheriffs Act roster
pinpoint: Printed p. 2616, middle column; PDF page 14. Notice dated 21 February 1972, published 5 July 1973.
claims: Nine named sheriff offices with their courthouse addresses and bailiwicks. The ninth is the Peace River portion of Cariboo, not a ninth county.
limitations: Roster publication does not establish when each office was created, nor that all officers remained in post until the 1974 reorganization.

title: Sheriffs Act, RSBC 1960, chapter 355
pinpoint: Sections 2–4, especially section 4 requiring July Gazette publication of sheriffs, offices and bailiwick limits.
claims: Explains the statutory basis and scope of the Gazette roster.

title: Province of British Columbia: BC Sheriff Service history
pinpoint: 1974 history entry.
claims: The government identifies 1974 as the year the nine county sheriff offices were amalgamated into a provincial service.
limitations: Retrospective official account supplies the year, not an exact administrative order or day.

title: Statute Law Amendment Act, 1974, SBC 1974, chapter 87
pinpoint: Assent on printed p. 535/PDF p. 1; section 35 on printed p. 547/PDF p. 13; section 42(1) on printed p. 550/PDF p. 16.
claims: Section 35 replaced geographically restricted jurisdiction with province-wide jurisdiction for each sheriff. It took effect on Royal Assent, 20 June 1974.
limitations: This is the jurisdictional reform. Its text does not itself amalgamate nine offices or prove the administrative merger occurred on 20 June.

title: Legislative Assembly Hansard, 20 June 1974 afternoon
pinpoint: Pages 4318–4319, debate on sheriff jurisdiction and court security.
claims: Attorney General explains that sheriff authority should continue across county boundaries and describes court security and prisoner transportation responsibilities.
limitations: The web page title mislabels the year as 1973; the session/date header and body identify 1974.

title: Legislative Assembly Hansard, 6 June 1974 night
pinpoint: Page 3809.
claims: Contemporary discussion describes the new sheriff service within the Attorney General department, a first trained class of approximately 35, and expansion plans.

title: Coastal Ferry Act, SBC 2003, chapter 14
pinpoint: Royal Assent header; sections 2(1), 2(4), 3, 20(3), 21.01 and 89.
claims: Royal Assent 27 March 2003; Act effective 1 April 2003; section 2 establishes B.C. Ferry Authority as a corporation without share capital. Section 20(3) ends the operator’s Crown agency upon conversion.
limitations: Current consolidation includes subsequent governance amendments; use the 2003 version for initial board mechanics. The Authority and operator are separate entities.

title: British Columbia Ferry Commission: From 2003 onwards
pinpoint: Opening history paragraphs.
claims: The operator, British Columbia Ferry Corporation, converted on 2 April 2003 to British Columbia Ferry Services Inc.
limitations: Official regulator’s older site; the conversion day differs from the Authority’s statutory establishment day.

title: Homeowner Protection Act, SBC 1998, chapter 31, historical consolidation
pinpoint: Royal Assent header; section 3 establishing office; section 4 board.
claims: Act assented to 30 July 1998; section 3 creates the Homeowner Protection Office when brought into force.

title: Homeowner Protection Act, Table of Legislative Changes
pinpoint: Entries for original sections 1–5, 6 and 7–13.
claims: Sections including section 3 came into force on 21 September 1998 under B.C. Reg. 309/98.
limitations: B.C. Reg. 309/98 is a regulation number, not Order in Council 309/1998.

title: Homeowner Protection Office, 2003/04–2005/06 Service Plan
pinpoint: Printed p. 3, PDF p. 7.
claims: The Office opened on 1 October 1998.
limitations: The plan’s July 28 passage date should not replace the Act’s July 30 Royal Assent date.

title: British Columbia Gazette, 21 December 1961: Pemco Holdings Ltd. incorporation
pinpoint: Printed p. 2290, right column, No. 52129; PDF p. 50.
claims: Pemco Holdings Ltd. was incorporated under the Companies Act on 13 December 1961, company No. 52129.
limitations: Gazette notice is the published registrar evidence; the underlying certificate itself was not obtained. OCR incorrectly renders the page number; the image reads 2290.

title: British Columbia Gazette, 27 May 1976: Pemco name change
pinpoint: Printed p. 715, right column, No. 52129; PDF p. 17.
claims: Pemco Holdings Ltd. changed its name to British Columbia Housing Corporation on 7 May 1976. The notice repeats its 13 December 1961 incorporation date.

title: British Columbia Gazette, 13 January 1977: PRHC name change
pinpoint: Printed p. 42, middle column near bottom, No. 52129; PDF p. 14.
claims: British Columbia Housing Corporation changed its name to Provincial Rental Housing Corporation on 21 December 1976; it is the same company incorporated 13 December 1961.

title: BC Corporate Registry credentials via OrgBook BC: BC0052129
pinpoint: Corporate registration credentials 60541, 60692 and 60731, effective dates and revoked_at boundaries.
claims: Registry corroborates the 1961 incorporation and both 1976 name changes, preserving the same company number.
limitations: Event timestamps should be displayed as local calendar dates. CONV-prefixed events are migrated historical registry events, not later reincorporations.

title: Auditor General of British Columbia, 1999/2000 Report 8: Social Housing
pinpoint: Printed p. 60 (PDF p. 55) for Province acquisition in 1973; printed p. 35 (PDF p. 30) for 21 July 1999 ministry reassignment; pp. 24–25 and 59–62 for separate governance.
claims: Province acquired the housing company in 1973. Both BC Housing and PRHC moved from the Minister of Employment and Investment to the Minister of Social Development and Economic Security on 21 July 1999.
limitations: Gives only the acquisition year, not the exact 1973 date or transaction instrument. Historical use of the later name PRHC should not imply that name existed in 1973.

title: Legislative Assembly Hansard, 29 June 1976 morning
pinpoint: Page 3223, Hugh Curtis on Pemco Holdings and British Columbia Housing Corporation.
claims: Contemporary explanation of repurposing the previously inactive company for housing finance.

title: Provincial Rental Housing Corporation, Financial Statements 2022
pinpoint: Note 1 (printed p. 11) and note 6(b) (printed p. 15).
claims: PRHC was wholly owned by the Province and a Crown agent; BC Housing was a related entity under common provincial control and managed its properties.
limitations: This establishes the 2022 relationship, not the 2024 control change.

title: BC Housing, 2023/24 Annual Service Plan Report and audited financial statements
pinpoint: Financial statements note 1, printed p. 10/PDF p. 43; note 20, printed pp. 23–24/PDF pp. 56–57.
claims: Governance and board-appointment changes gave BC Housing control of PRHC on 26 January 2024. It elected to consolidate PRHC from 31 March 2024.
limitations: The audited note describes control through governance; it does not prove transfer of the Province’s shares. Web text omits these scanned financial-note pages; the original PDF page was visually checked.

title: Province of British Columbia, 2010 announcement of HPO integration
pinpoint: Effective 1 April 2010 division of responsibilities.
claims: HPO regulatory, research and education functions moved to BC Housing; reconstruction loan responsibilities moved to the Ministry of Finance.
limitations: Function transfers should be represented separately from legal abolition/commencement provisions in the amending Act.

title: Order in Council 1188/1998: Homeowner Protection Act commencement
pinpoint: Single-page signed order, approved and ordered 16 September 1998.
claims: Brings sections 1–13, 19, 24–29, 31–36 and 38 of the Homeowner Protection Act into force effective 21 September 1998.
limitations: BC Laws PDF was downloaded directly and visually verified; the web parser returned an access error and its error reference is not evidence.

title: Order in Council 1146/1998: assignment of statutory administration
pinpoint: Single-page signed order, approved and ordered 16 September 1998; Minister of Municipal Affairs row.
claims: Explicitly charges the Minister of Municipal Affairs with administration of the Homeowner Protection Act under Constitution Act section 10.
limitations: Assignment of statutory administration should be labelled as such; it does not automatically mean corporate share ownership.
